supermarket.note: The chilled pre-steamed packs sold three to a bag. Instant ramen blocks also work, see the troubleshooting notes.
Thin shabu-shabu slices cook in seconds. Bacon is a fine stand-in.

general.note: Bottled sauce is easiest. The sachet inside the noodle pack works too, and one sachet is about 2 tbsp.

optional.note: A small shaker lasts years and it is what makes a plate smell like a festival stall.
Sharp and sour against the sweet sauce. Worth picking up if you see a jar.

tools.name: Lid
tools.note: A plate laid over the pan does the same job.

steps.title: Cut vegetables
points: Cut the cabbage into rough 3 cm squares, the onion into thin wedges, and the carrot into thin strips.
Keep the carrot thinner than everything else, it is the slowest to soften.
Pile it all on one corner of the board so you can tip it in at once.

steps.title: Cut pork
points: Cut the pork slices into pieces about 4 cm wide.
Long strips tangle in the noodles later and come out in one clump.

steps.title: Loosen noodles
points: Open the pack and pull the noodle brick apart with your fingers.
They come out compressed and stuck together, and separating them dry is much easier than fighting them in a hot pan.
steps.hint: If the block will not budge, put it on a plate and microwave it for 30 seconds. The steam inside loosens it.

steps.title: Brown pork
points: Heat the oil over medium-high, then spread the pork in one layer.
Cook about 2 minutes without moving it, until the edges are browned.
Season it with a little black pepper here.

steps.title: Add vegetables
points: Tip in the carrot, onion, and cabbage together.
Toss for 2 to 3 minutes, until the cabbage has wilted but still has bite.
The pork fat coats everything, so nothing should stick yet.

steps.title: Steam noodles
points: Lay the loosened noodles over the top, pour the water around them, and cover.
Leave it 1 minute, then take the lid off and toss everything together.
The noodles should be hot, glossy, and moving freely.
steps.hint: The water is there to steam the noodles, not to boil them. If the pan still has liquid pooling after a minute, cook it off before the sauce goes in or the sauce will taste watered down.

steps.title: Add sauce
points: Pour the yakisoba sauce around the edge of the pan, not onto the noodles.
Toss hard for about 1 minute, until every strand is the same brown.
Let it sit still for the last 20 seconds so the sauce catches on the pan and turns fragrant.
steps.hint: Sauce hitting bare hot metal caramelises. Poured straight onto the pile it just soaks in and stays flat.

steps.title: Plate
points: Pile it onto a plate while everything is still steaming.
Add a pinch of aonori and a small heap of pickled ginger on the side if you have them.
Grind over more black pepper and eat it straight away.

troubleshooting.problem: The noodles broke into short pieces
troubleshooting.solution: They were tossed too hard while still cold and stiff. Give them the full minute under the lid first, and turn them over from underneath with chopsticks instead of stirring in circles.

troubleshooting.problem: The noodles stuck to the pan
troubleshooting.solution: The pan ran dry between the vegetables and the sauce. A splash more water frees them immediately, and next time add the sauce as soon as the noodles are hot.
Too much water went in, or the cabbage released a lot. Cook uncovered for another minute before the sauce so the liquid boils away.
Mix 2 tbsp worcestershire sauce, 1 tbsp ketchup, 1 tsp soy sauce, and 1 tsp sugar. It lands very close. Oyster sauce in place of the ketchup makes it rounder.

troubleshooting.problem: Only instant ramen in the cupboard
troubleshooting.solution: Boil the block for a minute less than the packet says, drain it well, and use it in place of the fresh noodles. Throw the soup sachet away, the yakisoba sauce is the seasoning.
Fry an egg in the empty half of the pan at the end and slide it on top. A soft yolk stirred through the noodles works like a sauce.
